facts.raw_span: a several-week history of a progressively enlarging swelling on the posterior ulnar aspect of her right forearm
no history of trauma
no systemic symptoms
a firm, non–tender 4 × 5 cm mass was palpated in the subcutaneous tissues of the distal forearm
no overlying skin changes
Neurovascular examination of the hand was normal
Plain radiographs of the forearm showed no fracture
soft-tissue swelling with cortical irregularity of the adjacent ulna
MRI of the right forearm revealed a mass arising from the bone and extending into the soft tissues
the lesion was isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images and heterogeneous hyperintense on T2-weighted images
marked enhancement after gadolinium administration
cortical bone lysis with medullary involvement

concepts.why: The presence of a mass arising from the bone with cortical bone lysis and medullary involvement, as seen on MRI, is highly suggestive of osteosarcoma, a malignant bone tumor.
The imaging findings of a mass arising from the bone with soft tissue extension and marked enhancement after gadolinium administration are consistent with Ewing's sarcoma, a malignant bone tumor.
The presence of a mass arising from the bone with cortical irregularity and soft tissue extension, as seen on MRI, could be consistent with chondrosarcoma, a malignant cartilaginous tumor.

The imaging findings of cortical irregularity and soft tissue swelling could be consistent with osteomyelitis, an infection of the bone, although the absence of systemic symptoms and the presence of a mass make this diagnosis less likely.

The presence of a mass arising from the bone with soft tissue extension and cortical bone lysis could be consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis, a rare disorder characterized by the proliferation of Langerhans cells.

frontier_selector.rationale: The mass arising from the bone with cortical bone lysis and medullary involvement, along with the imaging characteristics, are most consistent with a primary bone malignancy such as osteosarcoma.
